en: The Ritual for the Accomplishment of the Great Yakṣiṇī Hārītī, Mother of Delight and Her Beloved Sons;
also known as the Sūtra of the Mother Hārītī.
[Compiled by] Suo Guo... [Title of Official Rank].

The Imperially Enfeoffed Lord of Three Thousand Households, invested with the purple robe and posthumously granted the title of Minister of Works, posthumously titled Dajian (Great Mirror), bearing the name Dayangzhi (Great and Vast Wisdom), the Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of Daxingshan Monastery, translated by imperial decree: At that time, the Buddha was dwelling at the Bamboo Grove Monastery in the city of Rājagṛha.
He expounded the essential points of the Dharma for the sake of the devas and humans.
At that time, there was a great yakṣiṇī named Ānandā,
whose appearance was upright and majestic.
She has five thousand followers who constantly reside in the land of China to protect and sustain the world;
she is the daughter of the yakṣa general Sāta.
The great yakṣa general Pāñcika— formerly called Sanji, which is a corruption— begot five hundred sons.
Possessing great majestic power,
he came to the place where the Buddha was with his retinue and sat to one side.
The Buddha said to Mātṛmodā:
"You should now receive the Tathāgata’s instruction.
I wish for you to abandon your violent and evil ways and to protect all sentient beings."
"In this city of Rājagṛha and throughout Jambudvīpa,
I grant fearlessness to all children, both male and female, born of women. At that time,
the mother Praharṣiṇī addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One, if it is thus, where shall I and my sons eat?
The Buddha said, “You need only maintain a heart of loving-kindness and not harm sentient beings;
I shall instruct my śrāvaka disciples.”
At every mealtime, I shall always give you food; furthermore,
at the end of the meal, I will set aside a portion of food and call out your name along with those of your children, ensuring that all of you are fully satisfied.
"If there is any remaining food, you may offer it in turn to all the spirits and deities,
directing your mind toward them so that they are all fully satisfied.
At that time, the Mother of Joy addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, I now take refuge in the Tathāgata.
I respectfully receive Your Buddha’s command and dare not transgress it.
As for the great city of Rājagṛha and all other lands..."
I shall protect all sons and daughters born among the people,
causing them to dwell in peace and happiness,
and ensuring that no malevolent ghosts or spirits may find an opportunity to harm them.
“I only pray that the Tathāgata will protect and mind me.
The Buddha said, “Excellent, excellent, Mother of Joy!
You may now [enter] into the well-expounded Dharma and Vinaya of the Tathāgata.”
Receive and uphold the Three Refuges and the Five Precepts, so that you may be liberated from all sufferings throughout the long night and attain great peace and happiness. These are:
taking refuge in the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Sangha; and abstaining from taking life.
"Even abstaining from all intoxicants is your training rule;
you should receive and uphold it.
At that time, the mother Prahlāda, having received the three refuges along with the five training rules, [was established].
Filled with joy and leaping for gladness, he circumambulated the Buddha three times and addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One, I have now received the protection of the Tathāgata.
I possess a *dhāraṇī* of my own mind."
It can eliminate all calamities, disasters, and terrors.
If there are those who receive and uphold these verses,
I and my retinue shall constantly provide protection for them, causing them to attain peace and happiness.
"I only pray that the Tathāgata will grant me leave to proclaim this.
The Buddha said, "Speak as you wish.
Thereupon, the Mother of Joy (Nandīmatr) spoke the dhāraṇī before the Buddha, saying:
Namo ratnatrayāya | Nama āryaiḥ | Mahāyakṣiṇyai | Homakāyai | Sattvānandinī | Mū...

Parivarta (26) nītrāṭi (27) sarvakarmakaraṇaye svāhā (28). Blessed One,
this dhāraṇī of mine possesses great power.
Just like a cintāmaṇi jewel,
which can fulfill all the wishes and aspirations of sentient beings,
may only the Tathāgatas and the Bodhisattvas bear witness to me.
The Buddha said, "Mother Ānandā, you have been able to benefit sentient beings by upholding my Dharma and reciting this dhāraṇī.
In future ages, among all my disciples..."
"I entrust you with their protection so that they may all be made peaceful and happy.
Then the Mother Joyful addressed the Buddha, saying,
"I shall carry out the holy instructions of the Buddha accordingly."
World-Honored One, if one wishes to accomplish this dharani rite,
one should first, upon a white cotton cloth or silk fabric,
according to its size, paint my image as Māmakī.
She takes the form of a celestial maiden, exceedingly beautiful;
her body is white and red, and she wears divine silken garments and precious jewels.
Her head is adorned with a crown, her ears with earrings, and her wrists with bracelets made of white conch shells.
Adorned with various kinds of necklaces and ornaments,
he sat upon a precious preaching throne and lowered his right foot;
on both sides of the throne, [there were...]
On either side of her knees, draw two children.
Her mother holds one child in the crook of her left arm against her breast, named Piṅgala,
making him appear exceedingly handsome.
The palm of her right hand, near her breast, holds an auspicious fruit (*śrīphala*).
To her left and right, paint her female attendants and retinue;
some hold white lotuses, while others hold ornaments.
The person who paints the image should bathe until pure,
don new clean garments, observe the eight precepts, and,
having painted it according to the Dharma, place it in a single private room.
Having cleanly swept and sprinkled the ground, construct a square mandala measuring four cubits on each side.
One should take the pure-colored *gomaya* (cow dung) of a female cow,
catch it in a vessel, and blend it with incense.
Having smeared and wiped it according to the Dharma,
one should further prepare a circular altar upon the square altar using white sandalwood paste. Place the image in the center,
provide a celestial canopy above, and suspend various multicolored banners.
Scatter various seasonal flowers upon the altar.
Furthermore, offer milk-rice, curd-rice, sweet and crisp foods,
as well as various fruits and *argha* water with fragrant perfumes.
Having burned agarwood as an offering,
the image faces west. The practitioner stands at the western side of the maṇḍala facing east toward the image and performs the recitation.
One should practice during four periods, three periods, or even just one period, without interruption;
if there is a break in the continuity, the rite will be difficult to accomplish.
Furthermore, one must not recite mantras of the Vajra family or engage in various other miscellaneous recitations.
It may be difficult to achieve success;
therefore, one should regularly recite it one hundred and eight times at each session.
While reciting with right mindfulness, one must not engage in casual conversation with others, lest it cause an interruption in the mantra.
If it is not accomplished, one’s efforts will be spent in vain.
If one wishes to achieve this rite,
one should begin on the first, fifth, sixteenth, or twentieth day of the waxing moon.
Recite [the mantra] before this image according to the aforementioned ritual procedure;
once ten thousand recitations are completed, the preliminary practice is accomplished.
You must maintain strict secrecy and not allow others to witness it.
Know that you must not recite this mantra in the presence of others.
If you can practice it with focused concentration according to the instructions,
the Mother of Joy will surely manifest her form.
It fulfills the aspirations of the practitioner.
When performing this recitation, one must certainly not harbor enmity toward others,
for fear of harming them and causing them disadvantage.
Once you have attained accomplishment, whatever wealth and treasures you obtain must be extensively distributed as acts of charity; you should not be stingy or miserly.
If you wish to cause the Mother to swiftly appear before you in person, [you should proceed as follows].
The practitioner should single-mindedly visualize this Mother as never departing from their heart.
Furthermore, at the place of recitation as well as one's dwelling,
it must be kept pure and no lamps or lights should be used.
Furthermore, one should constantly burn aloeswood incense.
Remaining alone in solitude, one should perform recitation without interruption;
nor should one feel any fear.
The Mother of Joy will certainly manifest her form.
Once she has appeared, if one were to let it be known to others, it would surely bring about calamity;
even when she manifests her form, one should not engage in conversation with her.
Simply recite with a sincere mind and further perform offerings according to the Dharma;
thereafter, [the deity] will surely come several times to address the practitioner, saying: "What should I do?"
If one leaves behind necklaces, bracelets, rings, or other precious ornaments,
they must be used immediately if necessary and may not be kept; furthermore,
one must not converse with them.
Only after she has been thus thoroughly matured over a long period may one speak with her;
one should then invite her to be either a mother or a sister,
and must not give rise to a mind of lustful attachment toward her.
If that noble one possesses a mind of defiled desire, he must certainly not accept it;
if he were to accept it, he would surely be born into that clan from which liberation is difficult to attain.
The practitioner of recitation, at every instance regarding his own food, [should maintain mindfulness].
First, set aside one portion of pure food.
Consecrate it seven times with the Heart Mantra.
Once finished eating, hold it and pour it out in a clean place.
One shall always receive protection and never be left alone by [the deity]. Recite the heart-mantra as follows:
Oṃ nurnu ma-biri-ka-hi-ti svāhā. Once the practitioner has completed the preliminary practices and the merit is fulfilled...
On an auspicious lunar mansion day, or during a solar or lunar eclipse, perform the ritual offerings according to the dharma;
take high-quality agarwood, dip it in ghee, and perform one thousand and eighty *homa* oblations. One will certainly attain accomplishment.
They may manifest their own forms,
or they may empower the rosary or the ritual implements,
in order to pray for the attainment of superior, middling, or inferior accomplishments.
If the ground upon which one resides shakes,
or if one beholds light, one should know that accomplishment has already been attained;
from this point forward, all that is undertaken will be realized as desired.
After employing these, for all subsequent methods of accomplishment:
if one seeks hidden treasures (*nidhi*),
one should take a maiden who has not yet reached puberty.
Having bathed for purification and donned fresh, clean garments,
take fragrant flowers and have a young girl hold them in both hands;
with her face veiled, she stands at the edge of the mandala.
The reciter shall chant the aforementioned mantra one hundred and eight times over saffron-scented water and sprinkle it upon the body of the young girl.
If one appends a petition for a specific objective to the mantra syllables,
that young girl will immediately reveal the location of the hidden treasure within a brief moment; or else,
one may simply recite the mantra with single-minded concentration.
Please request the Noble One to manifest his form so that you may inquire as to her whereabouts;
or simply pray that the Mother Who Delights be granted the daily provision of all necessities.
If this wish is fulfilled, whatever wealth and treasures are obtained [shall be offered].
One should extensively cultivate merit and practice the giving of alms to benefit sentient beings;
one must not hoard wealth, for it will inevitably cause the failure of one's accomplishments.
Furthermore, this dharma is intended to bring joy to noble persons.
Take earth from beneath that person’s door,
mix it with saliva to form a pill, empower it one hundred and eight times, and place it in their latrine;
that person will surely become respectful, compliant, and joyful.
Furthermore, if one wishes to gain the respect and affection of a woman,
empower twenty-one fruit kernels with mantras and give them to her to eat;
she will then feel mutual respect and love.
Furthermore, if there is a matter of doubt,
one should perform the empowerment as before upon a young girl and question her;
she will explain all the various points of the intended inquiry.
Furthermore, according to another method, one may simply perform recitation and offer prayers for specific requests;
then, either a voice from the air will communicate with one,
or during dreams, one will certainly be informed, thereby coming to know all matters of doubt.
Furthermore, according to another method, if one is possessed by malevolent spirits or afflicted by fear and anxiety,
take frankincense (*agaru*), asafoetida (*hiṅgu*), and white mustard seeds mixed with clarified butter (*ghṛta*).
Perform *homa* one thousand and eighty times, and all malevolent spirits will be entirely eradicated.
Furthermore, if there are wicked people who create obstacles,
take *rudrākṣa* seeds mixed with earth,
and empower them twenty-one or one hundred and eight times.
Bury it secretly beneath the threshold of that person's house.
If the one who creates obstacles falls ill, their illness will be cured as soon as they retrieve that soil.
Furthermore, there is another method for those whose spouses are in discord.
Regarding the clothing and other items he uses, or the food he eats,
empower them secretly twenty-one times and give them to that person for his use;
do not let him perceive it, and he will certainly find them agreeable.
Furthermore, there is a method: if someone has been poisoned, one should empower white pigeon droppings with water and give them to drink; they will be cured immediately.
Furthermore, there is a method: if there are those who have been imprisoned, shackled, or subjected to various verbal disputes...
On the fifth day of the fifth month, take a branch of peach wood and secretly write the name of that hostile person upon it.
Empower it one hundred and eight times with mantras.
Furthermore, if one recites the person's name within the mantra syllables and empowers words of petition by driving them into the ground,
then disputes with government officials will immediately be resolved and all matters will become peaceful.
Furthermore, if one wishes to achieve victory in debate,
take a piece of wild-ge grass (aconite), empower it twenty-one times with mantras,
and hold it in the hand while debating with the opponent; they will then be silenced.
Furthermore, for the case of a woman who has difficulty finding a husband:
fashion an effigy out of ash and empower it one hundred and eight times.
Command that woman to prostrate before this ash-effigy seven times every day.
In such marriages, ten thousand will succeed without missing even one.
Furthermore, if one wishes to summon a beloved person from afar,
one should fashion a figure out of ash, or it is also acceptable to make one out of salt.
Place a blade upon their heart and recite their name.
At each of the three periods of the day, perform the mudrā of summoning and invocation, and empower them by reciting the mantra one hundred and eight times.
Within no more than seven days, that person will arrive.
Alternatively, if they do not come, that person will surely suffer from a grave illness.
Furthermore, if there is one who owes a debt and does not repay it,
one should fashion an image of that person using salt powder.
Form the mudrā of subjugation and recite the dhāraṇī one hundred and eight times.
Within the phrases of the mantra, utter the name of that person and scratch it with a blade.
That person will immediately come of their own accord, prostrate themselves, and beg for their life.
Furthermore, according to another method, if a person suffers from a disease caused by malevolent spirits or demons,
one should perform the empowerment as previously described upon a young girl and question her;
thus one will know the actions of the demonic affliction causing the illness.
One should immediately expel those malevolent spirits by means of the Dharma;
there is no patient who will not be cured.
Furthermore, regarding the method for departing when one intends to treat illnesses:
First, light a single lamp and place it beneath the hearth.
Empower it twenty-one times with the mantra and then cover the hearth door.
At dawn the following day, go and inspect it.
If the oil is exhausted, then remove it.
If it is not exhausted, there is no need to treat it;
otherwise, recovery will certainly be difficult, for this method is extremely dangerous.
Furthermore, there is another method: during a solar or lunar eclipse, one should place clarified butter in a vessel of refined copper before the image and perform empowerment until it is full again.
By consuming this empowered butter, one will immediately attain the power of hearing and retaining, and shall recite a thousand words daily.
Furthermore, if there are those who are discordant or unyielding,
one may secretly recite the mantra to empower fruits or food and drinks;
by skillfully giving these to that person to eat, they will surely attain respect and affection.
Furthermore, regarding the method for any household where a death has occurred and which causes people to be terrified:
with a mind of wrathful intensity, recite this dhāraṇī twenty-one times or one hundred and eight times.
Terror will be immediately dispelled.
It is most excellent not to go to the house of death.
Furthermore, regarding the method for when one is involved in legal disputes before government officials:
Recite this mantra one hundred and eight times;
or, by reciting the mantra silently, one will certainly attain the desired result.
Furthermore, if one wishes to have an audience with a great personage or an official, [one should proceed as follows].
Recite the mantra one hundred and eight times;
upon seeing [the deity], one will certainly attain joy.
Furthermore, as for another method: if there is a woman who has difficulty in childbirth...
Consecrate cow’s ghee one hundred and eight times, or twenty-one times, and give it to the woman in labor to drink and apply it to her birth canal; she will certainly deliver easily.
Furthermore, if the practitioner recites this mantra with single-minded devotion and does not practice anything else, [the same result will be achieved].
The Mother of Joy will constantly follow and protect you, never departing from your side;
before long, she will surely manifest her form.
If one practices this rite of the Mother of Joy and desires to bring about swift results:
One must establish a separate, quiet chamber and maintain the utmost secrecy.
One must not perform the ritual within a Buddha hall or a vihāra,
for it is feared that success will be difficult to achieve.
Furthermore, one must not allow others to see this image or know the ritual procedure;
otherwise, its efficacy will surely be lost.
Moreover, if there is an enemy who intends to come and cause harm, [one should perform the following].
Take sesame seeds mixed with clarified butter and perform one thousand and eighty *homa* offerings before the image.
By reciting the person's name within the mantra syllables, they will certainly be made to rejoice.

Furthermore, there is a method: if one wishes to cause another person to remember oneself, one should write that person’s name and place it beneath the feet of one’s own bed; that person will certainly remember one.
Furthermore, there is a method: if one wishes to cause the household of an enemy to be terrified and unsettled, [one should perform the following].
Take a piece of skull bone and empower it twenty-one or one hundred and eight times.
Secretly place it within the residence of that enemy;
their household will surely become terrified and unsettled.
Whenever one wishes to take a skull bone,
first empower oneself with the mantra twenty-one times; then,
having formed the summoning mudrā (*ākarṣaṇamudrā*), one may take it.
Through secret empowerment, there is nothing that does not manifest as a miraculous response.
If one wishes to cause that person to be free from fear,
one should recite this mantra twenty-one times.
Collect the skull bones and perform the rite of dismissal (*visarjana*), returning them to their original location.
Thus, that household shall immediately attain fearlessness.
These bones may be used only once; they are no longer fit for reuse.
This is unproven.
Generally, once the meal has been finished through offering, all food including fruits and so forth must not be eaten.
This will cause the mantras held by the practitioner to be ineffective.
Whenever one intends to offer food to the Mātṛgaṇas (Mothers of Joy),
it is necessary to prepare fresh and distinct portions for each.
One must not use food that has been left over overnight.
Whenever one presents an offering of food, one must deliver it personally; it will certainly be ineffective if sent by another.
Furthermore, regarding the method for achieving the rite of command and service:
First, having completed the ritual practice by reciting the mantra,
one should then select a skull.
If it is known that this skull belonged to a person who was capable and diligent, [it is suitable].
One will certainly attain success with ease.
First, perform self-consecration at the site where one has seen [the skull].
Then, consecrate that skull one hundred and eight times with the mantra.
Forming the mudrā of invitation, summon them and cause them to follow you;
wrap them securely and bring them along.
First wash them with pure water, and then bathe them with scented water.
Using silver for the tongue, perform one hundred and eight empowerments before the Image of Joy.
Covering the head with a steamer over the side of the altar,
one’s own name will be revealed spontaneously during that very night.
Or he may manifest his body and request to serve as an attendant;
from that time forward, whatever tasks he is commissioned to perform will invariably prove effective.
Should one have doubts or questions, he will certainly be able to know them beforehand.
This dharma must be treated with extreme secrecy;
if it is leaked, not only will it fail to take effect, but it will conversely bring about misfortune and retribution.
Whenever one sends a skull to another person's location, [one must observe these precautions].
First, one must examine the person before them:
if that adversary is one who maintains the recitation of the Vajra Family dharmas,
or one who strictly observes the prohibitions and understands the dharma.
If you do not refrain from causing disturbance, it will instead bring harm upon yourself;
otherwise, the result will surely be effective.
Next, the mudrās are explained.
First, form the mudrā for summoning:
interlace the fingers of the right hand behind the back of the left hand,
grasping the palm of the left hand.
With the left hand, perform three beckoning gestures toward the body; thus the mudrā is formed.
Next, bind the subjugation mudrā by interlacing the two hands with the palms facing inward.
The two little fingers hook together.
The two ring fingers each enter the hollow of the wrist from the left and right respectively.
The two middle fingers are held upright and joined together.
The two index fingers each grasp the back of the middle fingers,
and the two thumbs each grasp the middle joints of the middle fingers;
thus the form of the mudrā is completed.
Next, perform the seal for casting out evil persons.
With the thumb of the right hand, press upon the nail of the ring finger;
with each recitation of the mantra once, cast it toward that evil person once.
The seal-form is thus completed.
Next, bind the seal for dispatching the Noble One;
that is, bind the previously mentioned seal of invocation and cast it outward with the right hand.
The seal is thereby accomplished.
At that time, the Mother Joyful, having spoken this dharani method within the great assembly, [concluded].
He addressed the Buddha, saying, "World-Honored One,
I have now received the Tathāgata’s protective mindfulness toward me.
I and my retinue shall respectfully carry out the Buddha’s instructions."
In future ages, they shall protect all sentient beings,
causing them to attain peace and happiness and to be free from all terrors.
If there are those who, relying upon this Dharma, purely receive and uphold this dhāraṇī, [they shall likewise be so protected].
All seekers shall have their desires fulfilled.
At that time, the Mother Praharṣiṇī again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, I shall now further proclaim the dharma of the *piṅgala-dhāraṇī* for one’s beloved son."
The mantra for benefiting and protecting all seekers is:
Oṃ citi citiṇi svāhā. As for the mudrā, join the two hands in the añjali gesture.
The two thumbs are bent together and inserted into the palms; thus it is formed.
This mudrā is used in all circumstances.
It is employed for summoning, making offerings, and sending away [deities] throughout the body.
One empowers one’s own five places with the mudrā—
namely, the crown of the head, the right shoulder, the left shoulder, the heart, and the throat— whereby the protection of the body is accomplished.
By beckoning with the two thumbs, it is called "invocation."
I hereby issue this name for your veneration.
If there are those who uphold this dharani method, I,
together with my beloved son Piṅgala and all our retinues, [shall provide protection].
I shall protect this person so that no evil ghosts or spirits may harass or disturb them.
If one holds this dhāraṇī, they must maintain purity and refrain from consuming anything tainted or defiled.
Recite the mantra three hundred thousand times and complete the offering of the *priyaṅgu* food for the beloved child; this constitutes the preliminary practice (*pūrvasevā*).
As for the method of making the food offering, first prepare it in a clean place in the open air.
Smear a circular mandala with cow dung;
scatter seasonal flowers upon it,
or it may also be performed simply upon a clean stone.
Whenever one wishes to eat,
first take a small portion of each food item and place them together in a clean vessel.
First, empower it seven times with mantras and place it upon that mandala; then,
call out the name of the *bṛhikā* and address her as follows:
"Please accept this food of mine and grant your protection.
In this manner, for a full six months without interruption,
he shall obtain his beloved son, who will always follow him and provide protection.
Furthermore, there is another method: either by begging for alms or consuming milk, one should recite the mantra three hundred thousand times.
Once this is completed, one may then prepare it using beef.
Perform one consecration and one burning three times every day;
for each session, recite [the mantra] one thousand and eighty times until forty-nine days are complete.
Then Piluṅka will manifest his own body and fulfill the practitioner’s aspirations.
Furthermore, there is another method: the practitioner should consume the three white foods and perform *homā* with pills made from beef mixed with *guggulu* incense,
beginning on the first day of the waxing moon and continuing for one full month.
Recite it one thousand and eighty times at each of the three periods of the day.
On the final day of the month, arrange extensive offerings.
For one full day and night, abstain from food and refrain from miscellaneous speech.
If one performs homa according to the instructions as described above, reciting with uninterrupted sincerity,
the beloved son Piluṅka will surely appear;
he will always be a close companion to the practitioner and shall provide whatever is required.
Furthermore, there is another method: take bright, pure, and high-quality *agaru* (sandalwood) incense,
dip it in clarified butter (*ghṛta*), and perform *homa* three times each day,
according to the aforementioned procedure for each session.
Thus, one should perform the homa without interruption or cessation,
constantly sending gold coins to provide for its requirements.
Furthermore, regarding the method for those who seek hidden treasures (nidhi):
Perform the preliminary rites as previously described.
Once they are completed, perform *homa* with *sugandha* mixed with clarified butter (*ghṛta*),
one thousand and eighty times for each of the three periods of the day.
In this way, without interruption or cessation,
that hidden treasure will immediately appear and may be taken and used without any obstacle.
If one constantly recites this dhāraṇī while also offering food, [the result will be as described].
It shall cause one's wealth and possessions to abound, and ensure that whatever is sought is obtained according to one's wishes;
one will then obtain this protection of Pṛṣṇigarbha. Furthermore, there is a method:
if one wishes to subjugate enemies, [one should perform as follows].
Write down the name of that enemy;
while treading upon it with the left foot of the reciter,
chant the mantra aloud with a wrathful visualization.
If one inserts the name of that enemy into the mantra and recites it one hundred thousand times, all adversaries will without exception become compliant.
Furthermore, there is a method for those who have been imprisoned:
By constantly reciting this dhāraṇī, one immediately attains liberation.
Furthermore, for those who wish to obtain peace and security,
take leaves of the *āmalaka* tree and mix them with milk.
By performing one hundred thousand empowerments through *homa*, one will immediately attain peace and security.
I shall now further explain the method for carving an image of Bhṛṅgī:
take a piece of fine white sandalwood that is free from flaws or cracks.
It should be six finger-widths or one span in length.
Have a skilled artisan carve it into the form of a youth,
with five topknots of vermilion and purple hair upon its crown.
With the marks and signs fully perfected, his body is adorned with various necklaces and ornaments;
he sits with his legs crossed upon a lotus leaf,
holding a śrīphala fruit in his right palm as if bestowing it upon others.
The practitioner raises the left hand with the palm facing outward and extends the five fingers downward;
this is called the "Hand of Fulfilling Wishes.
Having formed this image, one should remain in a clean and secluded room.
Mix asafoetida with scented water and clay to construct a square altar measuring one cubit or three cubits. Then,
smear it with cow dung according to the ritual rules.
Furthermore, smear a circular seat with white sandalwood incense and place the image upon it;
scatter various seasonal flowers upon the altar,
along with milk porridge, curd-rice, and sweet, crisp fruits.
Furthermore, perform offerings according to the ritual,
such as *modaka* cakes and other foods. Incense the *agaru* (aloewood) before this image and recite the dhāraṇī one hundred thousand times.
The beloved son Pilindavatsa will appear in person and ask the practitioner:
"Why have you summoned me? What do you seek?
Whatever the practitioner desires, they shall obtain it according to their wishes.
From this point onward, there shall be no ritual procedure that fails to produce its result.
Furthermore, regarding the method for knowing future events, whether auspicious or inauspicious:
take *gomaya* (cow dung) and smear the altar as previously described.
Perform the offerings as before.
Burn agalloch incense with sesame seeds;
consecrate each one once and burn them until the count reaches one thousand and eighty times.
Then, lie down to sleep in this very place without engaging in idle chatter.
With single-minded concentration, contemplate the holy deity Bhṛṅgī, requesting his visionary realm.
After a short while, you will see Bhṛṅgī in a dream; ask him about whatever doubts you have, and he will explain them all. The mantra for requesting the dream is as follows: [Mantra]
Oṃ dhara dhara, jamba jambha, stambhe hi hi, pṛṅkara, sarvasattvān vaśīkuru, ha ha hi hi hu hu svāhā. At that time, the Mother of Joy—
Having thus explained this *dhāraṇī* of one’s own mind and the method for accomplishing the beloved son Piṅgala,
he prostrated himself with his five limbs touching the ground and paid homage at the feet of the Buddha.
He addressed the World-Honored One, saying: "World-Honored One, I now employ this dhāraṇī and its methods of accomplishment to benefit sentient beings.
I only pray that the Tathāgata and the assembly of noble ones will bear witness to me."
The Buddha said, "Excellent, excellent, Mother of Joy!
I now entrust this further to you all within my Dharma."
In all monasteries where ordained disciples reside,
you and your retinue shall diligently protect them with a devoted mind,
ensuring that no malevolent spirits or ghosts create obstacles or difficulties, so that they may attain peace and happiness.
"Until my Dharma has ceased to exist,
you should act in this manner throughout Jambudvīpa.
At that time, the mother Praharṣaṇī and her five hundred sons [did so].
Together with their retinues, the yakṣas and other hosts,
having heard the Buddha’s command, all rejoiced greatly, paid homage, and departed.
